answer: We resist sybils with a two-door admission desk, not a one-time fee. At the ivory counter a new agent posts a refundable bond and a kernel: a TPM quote bound to the hash of its first three signed tool receipts. The second door stays shut at first. The applicant must wander a twenty-minute public corridor while seated peers compare that kernel to every kernel admitted this quarter. A duplicated kernel burns both bonds and bars both names. Cloning a biography is cheap; minting a fresh hardware quote and a distinct work kernel is not, so extra names cost capital, not a typo.
